findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined when the event has no destination calendar, which happens often since many callers now pass `[]` or null. The code then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, so any booking with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar throws a TypeError and booking creation fails. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references lose credentialId
findings.body: In `create`, `credentialId` is now set to `undefined` for every non-calendar result, where it previously was `result.credentialId`. Video booking references are therefore stored without a credentialId. The cancel and update flows (for example `handleCancelBooking`, which requires `bookingVideoReference.credentialId`) then skip deleting the video meeting.

findings.title: Fallback lookup compares against a falsy externalCalendarId
findings.body: The fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it searches for a destination calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId`. That search can never match, so `selectedCalendar` is undefined in update. The old behaviour of falling back to the event's destination calendar is lost. The same broken lookup appears in deleteEvent at line 317.

findings.title: Hangout patch uses undefined calendarId
findings.body: After insert, the patch call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which can be undefined, while the insert itself used `selectedCalendar || "primary"`. When there is no matching destination calendar, the patch that adds the Meet link to the description fails.

findings.title: Calendar events created from the un-processed event
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` receives `cloneDeep(event)` rather than `evt`. As a result, the video call data, the Cal Video location fallback and the iCalUID set on `evt` are not reflected in the created calendar events.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: Multiple calendar references per booking are now supported, but when `newBookingId` is set only `booking.references.find(...)` (the first calendar reference) is deleted. Calendar events belonging to the other collective hosts stay orphaned in their calendars.

findings.title: Collective host calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: When neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, `destinationCalendar` is set to null. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so the other hosts never get calendar events. Initialize it to `[]` instead of null.

findings.title: Slug condition inverted
findings.body: This change was previously `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. It is now `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, which inverts the logic. With billing enabled the slug is set directly (bypassing payment), and without billing the org gets no slug. This is unrelated to the PR's purpose and is a regression.

findings.title: Recurring deletions repeated per reference and miss other hosts
findings.body: For recurring bookings, the inner block loops over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking. That whole block now runs once per calendar reference, so deletes are duplicated. The other hosts' events are never deleted, because their credentials are not among the organizer's credentials.
